title: Preconception counselling components in women with serious mental illness: a scoping review.
abstract:
AIMS: Women with severe mental illness (SMI) face significant pregnancy-related risks, yet targeted preconception counselling (PCC) remains poorly defined. This scoping review systematically maps existing literature on PCC for women with SMI.
METHODS: Following the JBI evidence manual for Scoping reviews and the PRISMA-ScR guidelines, MEDLINE, Embase, PsycINFO, and Web of Science databases were searched from inception to June 2025. English-language articles describing PCC interventions or guidelines targeting women with bipolar disorder and psychosis-spectrum disorders were included.
RESULTS: From 1,208 unique records, 33 articles were identified and reviewed, predominantly narrative reviews ( = 23/33, 70%), clinical guidelines ( = 4/33, 12%), and empirical studies ( = 5/33, 15%). Key PCC themes included: Maternal and infant risks and lifestyle education ( = 28/33 articles), medication and treatment options ( = 27/33), planning and preventive care ( = 27/33), history-taking and risk assessment ( = 18/33), and multidisciplinary support/relational aspects ( = 14/33). Structured interventions or standardised frameworks were rare ( = 1/33), and articles infrequently addressed patient-centred factors or Infant Mental Health ( = 2/33).
CONCLUSION: Current evidence on PCC for women with SMI remains fragmented. The findings support the need for clearer, consensus-based guidance integrating psychiatric, reproductive, and psychosocial considerations, with IMH emerging as an underexplored author-identified area for future PCC framework development. Future research should prioritise prospective studies, development/assessment of structured interventions, standardised PCC frameworks, and expert consensus, to support accessible, stigma-free, and resilience-enhancing care for women with SMI, ultimately supporting optimal outcomes for mothers, infants, and families.

journal.name: JOURNAL OF REPRODUCTIVE AND INFANT PSYCHOLOGY
